title: Documented-Use Compliance for Continued Rental, Durable Medical Equipment Rentals
content:
Medical management review note - Durable Medical Equipment Rentals classes that require a compliance trial.

> Where the payment class requires a compliance trial, continued rental after the trial depends on documented use of at least the class's minimum nightly hours on at least the class's minimum percent of nights in a span of the class's number of consecutive days inside the class's compliance window, counted in days after delivery, read from the device's usage report. When compliance is not shown, the class's outcome for a failed trial applies and no rental month after the window is paid until the patient is re-evaluated in person and a new trial is passed.

The documented-use result of a trial is recorded on the placement as its compliance result.

## Elements of the test

| Element | What it is |
|---|---|
| Source of the evidence | The device's usage report |
| A qualifying night | A night with use of at least the class's minimum nightly hours |
| Measurement span | A run of consecutive days of the class's length |
| Where the span must lie | Inside the class's compliance window, counted from delivery |
| Pass mark | Qualifying nights make up at least the class's minimum percent of the nights in the span |
| Not shown | No rental month after the window is paid until an in-person re-evaluation and a new trial passed |

## Worked reading (hypothetical usage report)

For illustration, take trial figures of a minimum of 4 hours a night, 70 percent of nights, a span of 30 consecutive days and a window of 90 days after delivery. Seventy percent of 30 nights is 21 nights.

| Hypothetical usage within one 30-consecutive-day span inside the first 90 days | Share of nights | Compliance in that span |
|---|---|---|
| 21 nights at 4 hours or more | 70 percent | Shown: at least 70 percent |
| 24 nights at 4 hours or more | 80 percent | Shown |
| 20 nights at 4 hours or more | about 66.7 percent | Not shown in that span |

A night of exactly 4 hours counts as a qualifying night, because the minimum is "at least" 4 hours; a night of 3.9 hours does not. A span that runs past day 90 after delivery does not lie inside the window.

## When compliance is not shown

- Rental months after the window are not paid.
- Payment of rental months resumes only once the patient has been re-evaluated in person and has passed a new trial; both are required.
